title: Aspen, Colorado Travel Guide
overview: Aspen combines major attractions with regional outdoor access and historical sites.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Maroon Bells
thingsToDo.description: Maroon Bells refers to two peaks in the Elk Mountains near Aspen—Maroon Peak at 14,163 feet and North Maroon Peak at 14,019 feet—forming one of Colorado’s most recognizable alpine skylines. The mountains are composed largely of sedimentary mudstone that weathers easily, giving the range its distinctive coloration and unstable climbing reputation. The area lies within the White River National Forest and is accessed seasonally through transportation controls designed to reduce road congestion in the Maroon Creek valley. Because the peaks combine measurable elevation, geologic distinctiveness, and strict management policies, they represent more than a scenic backdrop. Maroon Bells illustrates how Aspen’s tourism economy is tied directly to high-elevation public lands and preservation rules.
